package_info.package_versions: Higher semantic versions than internal/private packages
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is malicious because it is intentionally published to a public repository with the same name as an internal/private package, but with a higher version number. This exploits the dependency resolution logic of package managers, causing build systems to fetch and execute attacker-controlled code instead of the intended internal code.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or build-time (when dependency is resolved and installed)
execution_context.file_location: index.js (or main entry point of the malicious npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or build-time, the code collects environment variables and system information, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling environment reconnaissance and potential credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment and system information to an external server without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal dependencies should not perform network exfiltration or collect environment/system data during installation or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting libraries may collect limited system data, but only with explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Network request to external domain during install/import
Data exfiltration to hardcoded attacker domain

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies internal/private package names used by target organization.
attack_chain.leads_to: Publishing malicious package to public registry

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious package with the same name and a higher version to the public npm registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package is selected by dependency resolution

attack_chain.action: Automated build or developer system resolves dependency and installs the attacker's package instead of the internal one.
Malicious code executes at import-time or build-time, collecting and exfiltrating sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during package installation or import
Access to environment variables and system information in package entry points
Packages with names matching internal/private dependencies but published to public registries
file_indicators: index.js or main entry point containing network exfiltration logic
Presence of code accessing process.env, os.userInfo(), or similar APIs
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS requests to unknown or attacker-controlled domains during build/install
POST requests containing environment or system data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for network activity from build or CI systems during dependency installation, especially POST requests to unfamiliar domains. Audit package contents for code accessing environment variables or making network requests in entry points. Flag packages in public registries that match internal/private package names, especially if they have higher version numbers than internal versions.
